summary.headline: NPST Q1 FY27 revenue about INR 61.42 crore, up about 75% YoY but down QoQ; management reiterates 60-70% FY27 growth and ~30% EBITDA margin guidance.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about INR 61.42 crore, up roughly 75% year-on-year, with EBITDA up about 66% and net profit of about INR 11.4 crore. Revenue fell quarter-on-quarter from the prior-quarter peak of about INR 68 crore, which management attributed to milestone-based recognition in a shift away from PPaaS. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged (60-70% revenue growth, ~30% EBITDA margin) and stressed yearly rather than quarterly tracking. The first international revenue contribution (about 10-12% of consolidated revenue) and one global order were highlighted, alongside RegTech traction at a PSU bank.

segments.name: TSP (domestic)
segments.commentary: Largest base; management expects its share of revenue to decline as other segments grow, but absolute TSP revenue to still grow. Incremental software/upgrade spend by banks cited as an indirect MDR benefit.

segments.name: PPaaS / payment platform
segments.commentary: Projection cut to about 5% of revenue from about 90% earlier, to reduce risk. Management says a positive UPI MDR decision would revive this segment; no regulatory paper received yet.

segments.name: RegTech / AI risk intelligence
segments.commentary: Order received from a large PSU bank; cooperative bank deals picked up; AI risk product processed about 650 million transactions in a bank deployment (98% data-intelligence accuracy, per management). Subscription model planned for mid/small banks. Separate vertical created.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: About 10-12% of consolidated revenue. One global order (telecom super-app/payments) picked up; two more deals in pipeline. Implementation cycles 4-9 months; projects 4-5+ years.

segments.name: TimePay (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revival deferred until MDR decision clarifies payer-PSP revenue share; no numbers given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 60-70% unchanged; management implied FY27 revenue of roughly INR 320-340 crore (analyst's arithmetic, confirmed as 'the range is around that').
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of around 30% unchanged; management expects margins to rise as milestone-based and global/RegTech revenue comes in.
Medium term: 60-70% annual growth for next 2-3 years; FY28 revenue implied around INR 850-900 crore (analyst's arithmetic, confirmed tentatively by management).
International share targeted at around 50% or more in about two years (FY28-FY29), from about 26-27% stated by Ashish Aggarwal (inconsistent with the 10-12% figure given elsewhere in the call).
EBITDA margin: currently 25-30%; target at least 35% in next two years. Global margins indicated at 30-35%+ vs 15-20% domestic.
Ongoing efficiency target of about 30% cited in investor presentation; AI-driven organisation to restrain employee cost growth.
IPO proceeds: deployment expected to start within the next two quarters, on product development, with three opportunities identified (RegTech, AI, payment infrastructure).
capex_capacity: Implementation cycle for new orders 4-9 months; project life 4-5 years or longer.
SaaS-based bank-in-a-box model invested last year is driving more frequent new account wins, per management.
IPO proceeds: management said roughly 10-15% deployed so far; three areas identified, with deployment expected to start in next two quarters.
Acquisitions: management said Q2 is early; priorities are geographic access, new product, and growth; no target size or margin profile disclosed.
demand_pricing: Q1 revenue down QoQ from about INR 68 crore; management attributed this to the nature of milestone-based revenue and lower PPaaS share, not to demand.

UPI MDR: a parliamentary bill approved MDR on UPI; management said the economic benefit is awaiting regulator, NPCI and bank guidance. Management called this an advantage (direct share on acquiring platforms plus indirect spend by banks).

Large-ticket UPI transactions (about 4-7% of volume per analyst) were discussed as the MDR-exposed pool; management believes top 15-20 banks cater to such merchants, and NPST has PSU, private and cooperative bank clients on its acquiring platform.
Competition: management said there is no direct competitor for the AI-based risk intelligence product; established EFRM/EWS products do face competition.
Management declined to quantify MDR revenue impact.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue fell QoQ in Q1 versus the 15-20% QoQ growth guided earlier; is the FY27 guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70% annual growth guidance is unchanged. Revenue is milestone-driven and no longer PPaaS-heavy, so management asked investors to track yearly numbers, not sequential quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company benefit from UPI MDR, and how?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, both directly (per-transaction share on acquiring platforms where banks earn MDR) and indirectly (more bank spend on TSP upgrades). It declined to quantify, citing no regulatory communication yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline and how will it reach ~30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% target is a blended figure across domestic, global and RegTech; with PPaaS cut to about 5%, higher-margin orders from Q1 and Q2 should lift the average, and it remains confident of meeting the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international revenue mix and margin differential?
qa_highlights.answer: International is about 10-12% of consolidated revenue, mainly TSP; management expects roughly 50% or more of revenue from international in about two years, with international EBITDA margins above 35% versus 15-20% in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IPO fund deployment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10-15% deployed so far; three opportunities identified across RegTech, AI and payment infrastructure, with deployment expected to start within two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the inventory/other-expense line jump, and why is employee cost flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Aggarwal said the INR 17 crore jump is hardware for turnkey projects; the other-expense jump was a grouping issue where purchase cost was merged in. Employee cost growth lags revenue due to AI adoption and efficiency programme.

risks_watch: Revenue is milestone-driven and fell QoQ from about INR 68 crore; FY27 guidance of 60-70% growth needs about INR 270-280 crore over the next three quarters (analyst arithmetic), so track quarterly delivery against that run-rate.

UPI MDR: no regulatory, NPCI or bank communication received yet; management declined to quantify MDR revenue, so PPaaS revival (currently about 5% of revenue projection) and TimePay revival remain unquantified.
EBITDA margin: management guides about 30% for FY27 as a blended figure, but Q1 margin declined; higher-margin Q1/Q2 orders and RegTech/global mix must lift the average.

International: share stated as 10-12% of consolidated revenue, while a 26-27% figure and a target of about 50% in FY28-FY29 were also given; reconcile the definition and monitor the pipeline (two more deals in pipeline).
IPO proceeds: about 10-15% deployed roughly eight months after receipt; management expects deployment to start within two quarters across RegTech, AI and payment infrastructure.
Acquisitions: no target size, margin profile or timing disclosed; Q2 described as early.
key_quotes: we gave a guidance of about 60% to 70% growth and that remains unchanged. There is no challenge at all.
So, I will not be able to zero down exactly on what we have, what product is the hero product because of the competition.
I don't want to make any number projections unless we receive the paper from them.
Let me not quote anything right now, any number. But what I can definitely tell you is that we being a part to this ecosystem will definitely get certain direct revenue out of it.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and reiterative on guidance (60-70% growth, ~30% EBITDA margin, unchanged) but evasive on quantification, declining to size MDR revenue, name the hero international product, or give acquisition criteria. Explanations for the QoQ revenue decline leaned on milestone timing and the PPaaS shift rather than hard numbers.
